title: Triad inversions
description: Root vs bass vs voicing, slash names, and the three inversions on strings 4–3–2.

cards.front: What does an inversion name?
cards.back: Which chord tone is the lowest sounding note — the bass.

cards.front: Name the three inversions of a triad and which tone is in the bass.
cards.back: Root position: root in the bass. First inversion: third. Second inversion: fifth.

cards.front: Write C major low to high in root position, first, and second inversion. Give the slash names.
cards.back: C E G = C. E G C = C/E. G C E = C/G.

cards.front: What is the difference between the root and the bass?
cards.back: The root is the note the chord is named and built from. It does not change when you invert. The bass is the lowest note actually sounding.

cards.front: How is voicing different from inversion?
cards.back: Voicing is the full arrangement: which strings, octaves, doublings, and omissions. Inversion only tells you which chord tone is lowest.

cards.front: What does the letter after the slash mean in C/E?
cards.back: The bass note, never a new root. C/E is still a C major chord with E in the bass.

cards.front: Why does a triad have exactly three inversions?
cards.back: It has three pitch classes, so there are exactly three possible bass notes.

cards.front: How do you get the next inversion by rotating the stack?
cards.back: Move the lowest note to the top, an octave higher. C E G becomes E G C, then G C E.

cards.front: What are the neighbor gaps in a major triad in each inversion?
cards.back: Root: M3 then m3. First: m3 then P4. Second: P4 then M3.

cards.front: What are the neighbor gaps in a minor triad in each inversion?
cards.back: Root: m3 then M3. First: M3 then P4. Second: P4 then m3.

cards.front: Check C minor first inversion E♭ G C. Name the two neighbor intervals.
cards.back: E♭ to G is a major third. G to C is a perfect fourth.

cards.front: Does inverting C major change the harmony?
cards.back: No. The pitch classes stay C E G. What changes is the bass, how settled it sounds, and which notes sit nearby.

cards.front: You play E G C on the top strings while a bassist plays C. What inversion is sounding?
cards.back: Root position. Inversion is about the lowest sounding note of the whole sound, not your shape’s nickname.

cards.front: Which inversion is most stable, and how does second inversion often feel?
cards.back: Root position is most stable. Second inversion often sounds unsettled and appears as a passing chord or a cadential tonic approaching V.

cards.front: What bass notes do D/F♯ and G/B ask for? What stays the root?
cards.back: Bass F♯ and B. Roots stay D and G.

cards.front: Give G major on strings 4–3–2 in all three inversions (frets and notes).
cards.back: Root 5 4 3 = G B D. First 9 7 8 = B D G. Second 0 0 0 = D G B.

cards.front: Slide the second-inversion shape 0 0 0 to 5 5 5 and to 7 7 7. Name the chords.
cards.back: 5 5 5 is G C E = C major second inversion. 7 7 7 is A D F♯ = D major second inversion.

cards.front: Give G minor on strings 4–3–2 in all three inversions.
cards.back: Root 5 3 3 = G B♭ D. First 8 7 8 = B♭ D G. Second 12 12 11 = D G B♭.

cards.front: On strings 4–3–2, where is the root in each inversion?
cards.back: Root position: lowest note (string 4). First inversion: top note (string 2). Second inversion: middle note (string 3).

cards.front: Give C major on strings 4–3–2 in all three inversions.
cards.back: Root 10 9 8 = C E G. First 14 12 13 (or 2 0 1) = E G C. Second 5 5 5 = G C E.

cards.front: Name chord and inversion: B D G (bass B); A D F (bass A); E♭ G C (bass E♭); D F♯ A (bass D).
cards.back: G major first inversion; D minor second inversion; C minor first inversion; D major root position.

cards.front: Write slash names: E G C; G C E; D F♯ B; A D F♯.
cards.back: C/E, C/G, Bm/D, D/A.

cards.front: Slide 0 0 0 to 3 3 3. Name the notes and the chord.
cards.back: F B♭ D. B♭ major in second inversion — bass F is the fifth, root B♭ is the middle note.

cards.front: Find first-inversion D major (F♯ A D) on strings 4–3–2.
cards.back: 4 2 3: string 4 fret 4 F♯, string 3 fret 2 A, string 2 fret 3 D.

cards.front: Why is a G chord with B in the bass still G and not Bm?
cards.back: The pitch classes are still G B D. A B minor chord needs B D F♯.

cards.front: Write all three inversions of F major and A minor.
cards.back: F: F A C, A C F, C F A. Am: A C E, C E A, E A C.
